answer: In PoA, trust propagates through bounded-length random walks on the attestation graph, with transition mass damped at each step to limit distant influence. A sybil cluster typically attaches through a sparse external cut, yielding low conductance and rapid internal mixing but weak escape probability. Cheeger-style bounds therefore cap its aggregate voting weight; even a velvet tide of identities cannot cross the ledge of honest attestations without proportionate trusted support.
